taxonomy.name: Access
taxonomy.q: Can an agent get in and read the raw response?
taxonomy.body: Crawler reachability, AI-bot rules, no JS-only wall, no login wall, clean redirects, Web Bot Auth.

taxonomy.name: Discovery
taxonomy.q: Can it find the map of your site?
taxonomy.body: robots.txt (+ Content Signals), sitemap.xml, RFC 8288 Link headers, llms.txt with a 'when to use' section.

taxonomy.name: Identity
taxonomy.q: Can it tell who you are and trust you?
taxonomy.body: JSON-LD (Organization + WebSite), real About / Contact / Pricing pages, complete metadata, brand discoverability.

taxonomy.name: Usability
taxonomy.body: Server-rendered content, markdown content negotiation, agent-friendly 404s, page token budget, accessible structure.

taxonomy.name: Capabilities
taxonomy.q: Can it DO something — call you?
taxonomy.body: Public API + OpenAPI / API Catalog, MCP server + MCP Server Card, Agent Skills, WebMCP, function-calling schemas.

taxonomy.name: Commerce
taxonomy.body: Agentic-checkout discovery: x402 payments, OpenAI's ACP, Google's UCP. Only if you sell.

taxonomy.name: Behavioral overlay
taxonomy.q: Can a real agent actually complete a task on your site?
taxonomy.body: The outcome test no checklist captures — and the one that matters. A perfect static score with a failed task is still a failure. Validate with a real agent run.

ladder.body: JS-only shell, blocked crawlers, no sitemap. Your content doesn't exist to an agent.
Server-rendered HTML, robots + sitemap, real 404s. The door is open.
llms.txt, JSON-LD identity, trust pages. An agent can represent and trust you.
Markdown content negotiation, clean structure, sane token budget. Low friction, low cost.
Public API + OpenAPI + MCP server. You go from a page an agent scrapes to a tool it invokes.
Agentic commerce (x402 / ACP / UCP). An agent completes a purchase without a human in the loop.

steps.s2: Server-render (or SSG) the meaningful content so it's in the raw HTML. The single biggest cause of L0.
Explicitly welcome AI crawlers (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended). Declare usage preferences with Content Signals.
A complete sitemap with lastmod. Add Link headers pointing to canonical and alternates.

steps.s1: llms.txt with a 'when to use this' section
steps.s2: The underrated one. Tell agents your best-fit use cases and key URLs in plain markdown at /llms.txt.
Never return 200 with your app shell for missing paths — it tells agents every URL exists. Add a short body linking to the sitemap.
Machine-readable identity on the homepage — name, url, description, contactPoint, isAccessibleForFree. Agents parse this, not your hero copy.
Agents check these to decide you're legitimate before recommending you. 500+ chars each; a real pricing answer (even 'free').
canonical, lang, og:image, og:type. Used for entity resolution and attribution.

tiers.title: Usability
tiers.eff: ~ half a day · cheap to be early

steps.s2: Serve text/markdown when an agent sends Accept: text/markdown, with Vary: Accept. Only ~4% of the top web does this — cheap differentiation.

steps.s1: Keep pages within an agent token budget
steps.s2: Split oversized pages so extracted text fits a context window (~25K tokens). Agents read the text, not the raw HTML.
One H1, sequential headings, landmarks, accessible names on controls, no div-soup. Good a11y is good agent-readiness.

steps.s1: A public, read-only API + OpenAPI spec
steps.s2: If your product is data (a catalog, index, docs), expose it as JSON with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec at /openapi.json — operationIds enable function-calling. Generates the API Catalog.

steps.s1: An MCP server + MCP Server Card
steps.s2: Expose read-only tools over Model Context Protocol so agents call you natively. Publish an MCP Server Card for discovery. Fewer than 15 sites globally have one.
Publish a Skills index or WebMCP tools for in-page agent actions. Emerging, but early.

tiers.title: Commerce — the frontier
tiers.eff: a project · only if you sell

steps.s2: Publish discovery files for agent payments: an x402 endpoint, OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). Lets an agent buy without a human.

glossary.def: A markdown file at /llms.txt telling agents what your site is and when to use it.
Directives in robots.txt declaring how AI may use your content (search / train / etc.).
Cryptographic signatures that let good agents prove identity so you can allow them.
HTTP Link headers exposing canonical/alternate relationships to non-HTML clients.
Schema.org structured data an agent parses for your identity and offers.
Model Context Protocol server exposing tools agents call natively; the Card advertises it.
A machine-readable API spec (operationIds) enabling agent function-calling.
A published index of discrete actions an agent can perform on your site.
In-page MCP tools letting an agent act within the browser context.
An HTTP-native payment endpoint standard for machine-to-machine payments.
Agentic Commerce Protocol — discovery + checkout for agent purchases.
Universal Commerce Protocol — Google's agentic-commerce profile.
